title: NOAA: added CO2 makes seawater more acidic by forming carbonic acid
summary: Ocean acidification is a chemical consequence of dissolved CO2, distinct from the temperature record.
body: NOAA's ocean-acidification page says carbon dioxide dissolved in seawater forms carbonic acid, a weak acid that dissociates into hydrogen ions and bicarbonate, and that higher atmospheric CO2 means more CO2 dissolving into the ocean. This is a chemistry claim. It is not the same statement as "the surface is warmer." Impacts on shells and reefs are discussed by NOAA; this card stops at the reaction the page states.
